knowledge:
- key_parameters: karyoFile=path to a text file containing chromosome names and lengths to define the genome tiling ;; reps=number of subsampling repetitions for fitting the negative binomial distribution (default 100) ;; sampleSize=number of tiles to sample in each repetition (default 30000) ;; p=p-value threshold for identifying high-signal tiles (default 0.99) ;; cores=number of CPU cores to use for parallel processing (default 1) ;; maxGap=maximum gap size in base pairs to merge adjacent grey list regions (e.g., 16384)
- alternatives: ENCODE blacklists are universal, pre-calculated signal-artefact regions independent of cell line or factor, whereas greylistchip generates cell-line or sample-specific grey lists. The greyListBS function is a one-step alternative to the step-by-step workflow when a BSgenome object is available.
- when_to_use: Use prior to ChIP-seq peak calling to identify and remove reads in high-signal anomalous regions of input/control samples, which improves insert size estimation and reduces false-positive peak calls.
- pitfalls: Chromosome names in the karyotype file must exactly match the chromosome names in the BAM file. Using inappropriate parameters (like very low p-values or small sample sizes) can lead to abnormally high genome coverage (e.g., 5.5% instead of the typical ~1%).

workflows.name: step_by_step_karyotype
workflows.intent: Generate a grey list from a BAM file using a custom karyotype file via step-by-step execution.
input: karyotype_chr21.txt (text file containing chromosome names and lengths)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize GreyList object with karyotype file ;; 2. Count reads in genome tiles from BAM file ;; 3. Calculate read-count threshold using negative binomial fitting ;; 4. Generate grey list regions ;; 5. Export grey list to BED file
workflows.code:
library(GreyListChIP)
path <- system.file("extra", package="GreyListChIP")
fn <- file.path(path,"karyotype_chr21.txt")
gl <- new("GreyList",karyoFile=fn)
gl <- countReads(gl,"myBamFile.bam")
gl <- calcThreshold(gl,reps=10,sampleSize=1000,p=0.99,cores=1)
gl <- makeGreyList(gl,maxGap=16384)
export(gl,con="myGreyList.bed")

workflows.name: bsgenome_one_step
workflows.intent: Generate a grey list in a single step using a BSgenome package and a BAM file.
workflows.stages: 1. Load BSgenome package ;; 2. Run one-step grey list generation ;; 3. Export grey list to BED file
